newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour dismisses budget leak complaints.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour dismisses budget leak complaints.

text.p: A spokesman for Britain's ruling Labour party played down complaints by the Conservative opposition about purported leaks of Wednesday's budget.

The Conservatives' main finance spokesman, Peter Lilley, has demanded that Ann Taylor, leader of the House of Commons, make an emergency statement at 1430 GMT about confirmation of a report that the government would end tax relief on private medical care for elderly people.
"This is complete hot air when you actually look at the facts," a spokesman for the Labour party said.

He said Labour had made clear in the run-up to the May 1 election its intention to use the savings from scrapping tax relief on private medical insurance for over-60s to pay for a cut in value added tax on home heating bills to five percent from eight percent.

After Prime Minister Tony Blair confirmed the intention in a speech on February 8, the Conservative party said the measure would raise only 110 million stg -- not enough to fund the maximum 450 million stg cost of cutting VAT on domestic fuel.
It was, therefore, "preposterous" for the Conservatives to complain, the Labour spokesman said.

He said Labour had always made clear that its maiden budget would redeem four pledges -- to cut VAT on fuel, to end the medical insurance tax relief, to impose a windfall tax on privatised utilities and to leave income tax rates unchanged.

Lilley is also demanding answers from ministers about a report in the Financial Times that quoted an unnamed member of the government as saying Brown intended to press ahead with plans to cut dividend tax credits to pension funds.
